summary: KERNEL CONTEST: The Rome Statute (the fixed foundational treaty) read as establishing a universal mandate for international criminal justice versus read (often by non-state parties) as a conditional framework requiring strict sovereign consent. Each reading alters the authority grounding and the jurisdictional boundaries of the court[cite: 2, 3].

KERNEL CONTEST: The imperial lineage and divine mandate (a lineage-based commitment system) read by the Tokugawa shogunate as a purely ceremonial, delegating husk versus read by imperial loyalists as the sole legitimate, active sovereign authority. An authority-grounding contest where the exact same historical substrate is wielded to emit opposing institutional constraints[cite: 2, 3].

KERNEL CONTEST: Historical treaties (the codified legal kernels) read by settler-state legal regimes as finalized property transactions extinguishing sovereign rights versus read by Indigenous nations as living, relational pacts for shared territorial stewardship. The competing readings instantiate entirely different constraints with different beneficiary and victim sets[cite: 2, 3].

KERNEL CONTEST: The Israeli constitutional framework (Basic Laws) read via a judicial supremacy lens (where the Supreme Court holds the ultimate interpretive boundary) versus a parliamentary sovereignty lens (where the elected Knesset can legally override judicial review). The disagreement is strictly about which constraint exists to adjudicate legitimate state action[cite: 2].
